newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND PROVES POINT BOTH TO HIMSELF AND RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND PROVES POINT BOTH TO HIMSELF AND RIVALS.

text.p: French downhiller Luc Alphand assured both himself and his rivals that he is still a force on the slopes despite his disappointing world championships with the fastest time in World Cup training on Thursday.

The 31-year-old downhill World Cup champion, who crashed out of the world championship downhill in Sestriere this month, descended one of the most challenging mountains on the circuit in one minute 57.88 seconds.
Italian rival Kristian Ghedina, who is second in the downhill rankings, clocked the second fastest time, 0.48 of a second behind with his compatriot Pietro Vitalini third fastest in 1:58.44.

Alphand won on the tough Kandahar piste last year but after Sestriere he needs to bounce back to form quickly in the German resort where two super-G's are scheduled for Friday and Sunday in addition to Saturday's downhill.
Training times on the World Cup circuit can sometimes be misleading since some racers do not ski to their limits but Alphand went flat out because he needed to boost his self-confidence.

"I went faster than usual today because I needed to prove to myself that I was okay," the Frenchman said. "I had a week off after Sestriere but I managed to motivate myself for the World Cup straight away."

Alphand is also bidding to become the first Frenchman to win the overall World Cup title since 1968. He is just four points behind Norwegian Kjetil Andre Aamodt who clocked the 25th fastest downhill time of 2:01.01 but is a stronger all-round skier.
There are 11 races left in the World Cup programme, seven of which are speed events where Alphand has his chance to pick up points.
"I'm not thinking of the overall title," Alphand repeated on Thursday. "Aamodt's the favourite."

The weather was warm in the German resort on Thursday but organisers were confident the races would be able to go ahead. After cancellations in the past Garmisch has spent a great deal of money on snow-making machines in recent years.
